answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs whose results are checked against randomly assigned, hidden test cases; repeated identities do not multiply that influence. A verifier samples outputs and pays a bond only when they pass, while failed work forfeits the bond and reputation. Creating a plume of fake accounts therefore forces the attacker to fund many deposits and produce independently valid work, not merely register identities. The inlet of cheap account creation narrows to a basalt barrier of measurable capital and labor.
